lines.text: In 1987, one man bought an unlimited lifetime plane ticket â€”
and flew ten thousand times on the airline's dime.
See, American Airlines badly needed cash in the eighties,
so they offered a wild golden pass for two hundred fifty thousand dollars.
Unlimited first class, anywhere on Earth, forever.
Investor Steve Rothstein happily paid up,
then turned airports into his personal subway.
He flew to London just for lunch,
and even booked an empty companion seat under the name Bag Rothstein.
Over twenty years he racked up thirty million miles,
costing the airline twenty-one million dollars in free seats.
Eventually an airport agent walked up, confiscated his golden card,
and banned him for exploiting their own promise.
Only sixty-six people bought the pass â€” and Steve won the record.
